page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware crypto acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). System memory totals 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or discrete graphics accelerators are bundled with this instance type, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistence.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and 31.34 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression, both placing in the top quartile of tested instances. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates top-tier throughput at 2536.0 points. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the 2 physical core constraint: stress-ng multi-core performance registered 3990.58 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 26.13 GB/sec, placing both in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth tests showed 36.73 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 25.99 GB/sec for large block writes.

In real-world application benchmarks, static web serving reached 7.74 GB/sec and PassMark database operations scored 2863.53, both settling firmly within mid-tier averages. Redis SET throughput attained 5.71 million operations per second, constrained by overall memory subsystem performance and core count. Small-model LLM prompt processing (135M) clocked 417.8 tokens per second, but medium-tier (7B) model prompt processing dropped into the lower quartile at 31.47 tokens per second.

Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, high single-core frequency, and lack of bundled local NVMe storage, the D4s_v6 provides balanced cost efficiency for general-purpose computing needs. It is best suited for web serving, microservices, lightweight application backends, and burst-tolerant business logic where strong single-thread responsiveness is favored over heavily parallelized multi-core compute.
